title: fix: blackout matching fails when service/tags are NULL after update

findings.explanation: The code does not involve SQL queries, so there is no risk of SQL injection.

The code constructs a query that includes user-controlled inputs (`alert.create_time`, `alert.environment`, `alert.resource`, `alert.service`, `alert.event`, `alert.group`, `alert.tags`). While the query structure is improved, there is still a possibility that the query could be manipulated to access unauthorized data if the inputs are not properly validated or authorized.

evidence.content:
query = {
    'startTime': {'$lte': alert.create_time},
    'endTime': {'$gt': alert.create_time},
    'environment': alert.environment,
    '$or': [{'resource': None}, {'resource': alert.resource}],
    '$and': [
        {'$or': [{'service': None}, {'service': {'$not': {'$elemMatch': {'$nin': alert.service}}}}]},
        {'$or': [{'event': None}, {'event': alert.event}]},
        {'$or': [{'group': None}, {'group': alert.group}]},
        {'$or': [{'tags': None}, {'tags': {'$not': {'$elemMatch': {'$nin': alert.tags}}}}]},
    ]
}

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure that all user-controlled inputs are properly validated and authorized before constructing the query. Consider implementing input sanitization and access control checks.
